title: BitGo Supports Connectivity to Decibel, Powered by Aptos
summary: Institutional clients with BitGo self-custody wallets can now connect to Decibel, a decentralized exchange for spot and perpetuals trading built on the Aptos network.
body_markdown:
## Key Takeaways


-


Institutional clients with BitGo self-custody wallets can now connect to Decibel, a decentralized exchange for spot and perpetuals trading built on the Aptos network.


-


Connectivity works through WalletConnect on Ethereum and Solana, with support expanding to additional networks over time, and BitGo’s trading desk can also route eligible spot and perpetuals order flow directly to Decibel.


-


Existing transaction controls, including address whitelisting and multi-party approval workflows, carry through the trading process, so clients keep the same policy engine and approval steps they already use.


## The gap between custody and onchain markets


Institutions have held digital assets with regulated custodians for years. That part of the infrastructure is mature:[cold storage](https://www.bitgo.com/resources/blog/crypto-cold-storage-explained/) , multi-party approval, address whitelisting, and audited controls are standard practice for institutional clients.


Accessing onchain markets from that same custody setup has been a separate problem. Trading on a[decentralized exchange](https://www.bitgo.com/resources/blog/dex-trading-for-institutions/) typically means moving assets into a different wallet or adopting a new workflow, which can mean stepping outside the controls a client’s compliance and operations teams have already built and approved.


BitGo now supports wallet connectivity for its self-custody institutional clients to Decibel, a decentralized exchange for[spot and perpetuals trading](https://www.bitgo.com/resources/blog/crypto-derivatives-101/) built on the Aptos network. Clients can elect to access Decibel while keeping the keys to their BitGo-connected wallets and retaining the transaction controls they already have in place.


## How the connectivity works


With wallet connectivity live, institutions can connect BitGo self-custody[multi-party computation (MPC)](https://www.bitgo.com/resources/blog/mpc-crypto-wallets-multi-party-computation-security/) wallets to Decibel through[WalletConnect](https://www.bitgo.com/resources/blog/bitgo-introduces-walletconnect-for-self-custody-wallets/) . From there, clients can initiate trades directly from the Decibel interface and approve transactions through BitGo’s MPC infrastructure and[wallet policy engine](https://www.bitgo.com/resources/blog/crypto-policy-engines/) .


The workflow breaks down into three parts:


-


A client connects their BitGo self-custody MPC wallet to Decibel using WalletConnect.


-


The client initiates a trade from the Decibel interface, without moving assets into a separate wallet.


-


The transaction routes back through BitGo’s MPC infrastructure and wallet policy engine for approval, following the client’s existing controls. Existing controls, including address whitelisting and multi-party approval workflows, carry through the trading process rather than being replaced or bypassed.


Decibel itself is powered by the Aptos network, which provides the underlying blockchain infrastructure for the trading venue, including sub-second finality.


This builds on BitGo's broader push into institutional DeFi access, following its[recent integration with Narval to connect self-custody clients to Aave, Spark, and Tesseract](https://www.bitgo.com/resources/blog/bitgo-launches-institutional-defi-access-for-aave-spark-and-tesseract-via-narval-integration/?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=foundational&utm_campaign=institutional_defi_access_competitor) .


If you would like to learn more about connecting your BitGo self-custody wallet to Decibel,[get in touch](https://calendly.com/d/crmk-p2t-k78) .


## Frequently asked questions


### What is Decibel, and how does it relate to Aptos?


Decibel is a decentralized exchange for spot and perpetuals trading. It is built on the Aptos network, a Layer 1 blockchain that provides the underlying infrastructure for the trading venue, including sub-second finality.


### Which networks are supported at launch?


Wallet connectivity to Decibel is supported on Ethereum and Solana. Support is expected to expand to additional networks over time.


### What happens to my existing approval controls when I trade on Decibel?


Existing controls, including address whitelisting and multi-party approval workflows, carry through the trading process. Transactions still route through BitGo’s MPC infrastructure and wallet policy engine for approval.
